sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
| Attack pattern | Explanation |
| --- | --- |
| Request flooding | Excessive requests sent to the API |
| Long-prompt abuse | Extremely large inputs consume tokens |
| Long-output abuse | Requests trigger expensive generation |
| Agent-loop exhaustion | Agents repeat tool/model calls |
| Retrieval exhaustion | Expensive or broad RAG searches |
| Concurrency exhaustion | Too many simultaneous requests |
| Repeated retry loops | Failed requests repeatedly consume resources |

### Example: Agent loop exhaustion

Suppose an agent follows this workflow:

```text
Think → Search → Think → Search → Think → Search → ...
```

If there is no maximum iteration count, one user request could trigger many model and tool calls.

steps.label: Query
steps.narration: The user query enters the system and may need rewriting before search.

steps.label: Transform
steps.narration: Query transformation expands, rewrites, or decomposes the question to improve recall.

steps.label: Search
steps.narration: Dense and/or keyword search return candidate passages.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.narration: Fusion methods such as RRF combine rankings from multiple retrievers into one list.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.narration: A cross-encoder or LLM reranker reorders candidates for higher precision context.

steps.label: Context
steps.narration: Final context is budgeted, ordered, and injected into the prompt for grounded generation.
